C-ROOT-WINDOW.IntentSummary:
Author the execution for the approved, fingerprinted spec `.ngrace/changes/active/C-ROOT-WINDOW/spec.xml` and only within it; the plan conforms to the spec, it does not extend, narrow or reinterpret it. The three resolved `Clarifications` (`INV-ROOT-WINDOW-UNMOVED`, `INV-ROOT-WINDOW-ROUNDING`, `INV-ROOT-WINDOW-MODE-CEILING`) are the maintainer's rulings and are implemented as written, not as the runner-ups. Two tasks, split by failure-signature family: T-001 lands the chartered engine — the `--rewrite-roots` mode, the floored derivation at all four sites, the unmoved-genre window rule, and the normalising pass, all in `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts`, together with the two suite rewrites that engine change alone reddens and the new assertions that observe the engine's behaviours — T-002 mints the bundle's registry row into `docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/registry.xml`, rewrites the registry roots with the chartered mode, and extends the shipped payer-derivation baseline with the row's six minted tokens plus the row and payment assertions. ObservedWriteScope is exactly three files — `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts`, `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts`, and `registry.xml` (the row and the roots the mode rewrites). DurableScope is `<None />`: no graph module is written and no `src/` file is edited — do not mint a synthetic module.
Why two tasks and not one or three. The fix budgets bind per task (`FIX_SIGNATURE_REPEAT_BUDGET = 2`, `FIX_DISTINCT_SIGNATURE_BUDGET = 4`, `src/grace-cursor.ts:187` and `:193`, re-read at this plan's commit). The bundle's work falls into two failure-signature families over two different file sets. The engine family (T-001) carries exactly four distinct signatures a failed drive can produce — a mode refusal shape, a fractional persisted value, a clamped unmoved window, and a non-canonical gap shape — which fits the distinct-signature budget of four and would exhaust it if the row family's two (mint render shape, roots read-back) shared the same window. The row family is over a different file with different failure causes, so it gets its own budget window as T-002. Not three tasks: the suite edits are not a third family — each one is forced by exactly one other task's write and only passes after that write lands, so a suite-only task would put a red `bun test` at the engine boundary and violate F184 in both directions. Each task carries the suite edits its own writes force, which is the F184 discipline: every recorded `Verification` command passes at the stage it is meant to run, measured — the shipped suite is 69 pass / 0 fail at this plan's commit, 67 pass / 2 fail on the prototype engine before the row exists (the two engine-caused reds are exactly the two tests T-001 rewrites), and 66 pass / 3 fail after the close (the third red, the payer-derivation baseline, is the one T-002 extends). Every task boundary is a demonstrable milestone, driven as recorded below.
Why the engine change and its two suite rewrites are atomic (T-001). The engine change reddens `T-001 min not decorative: hand-shrunk findings persist ceiling = Base_live + H without a findings move` (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:738` — it pins the F193 clamp this bundle overturns) and `C-RECORD-PARSE golden: a fixture --retire writes byte-for-byte the files the shipped engine wrote at capture time` (`:1841`); conversely the rewritten `min not decorative` asserts window survival and only passes after the hold exists, and the re-captured golden only matches the chartered bytes. Separating them makes one boundary red no matter the order. The `T-001 window: persisting the findings snapshot after a move uses the pre-move base + H` test (`:658`) passes under the chartered engine unchanged (driven: the moving-genre arithmetic is kept, and on the driven fixture the floored headroom equals the unfloored one because the median is integral) — measured, and kept.
Why not a third, suite-only task, and why the new assertions split the way they do: the mode, floor, window and indent assertions observe the engine (T-001's family); the row, payment and pre-payment assertions observe the record with the row in it (T-002's family). No `Verification` command recorded below only passes after a later task lands: T-001's suite is green with the production record untouched (driven: the plan-time suite run at this plan's commit is 69/0 on the shipped engine and the fixture-based additions pass against the shipped engine's own fixtures), and T-002's additions pass with the row live (the payer derivation mints nothing from an unarchived row — measured).
The mapping, fixed by the spec's own Constraint (the trap that has cost supersedes): exactly one criterion — `AC-NO-CURRENT-MODE` — carries no `CloseEvidence` and is mapped by exactly one task `Satisfies`, carried by T-002, whose verification completes the plan's command set; it is this plan's only `Satisfies`, and no other task carries one. Measured basis at this plan's commit: `validateSpecPlanCoverage` (`src/artifact/grammar.ts:2049`) warns `change.acceptance-criterion-unmapped` for a criterion that is neither task-mapped nor close-bound, `isCloseBoundCriterion` (`src/artifact/grammar.ts:2142`) counts a criterion close-bound when it carries a complete `CloseEvidence` child, and `change.close-evidence-and-satisfied` (`src/lint/catalog.ts:286`) errors on a `Satisfies` of a close-bound criterion; eleven of this spec's twelve criteria are close-bound and `AC-CLOSE-LINT`'s `CloseEvidence` runs `--fail-on warnings`, which fails on any issue, so an unmapped `AC-NO-CURRENT-MODE` would make the bundle's own close unsatisfiable. Every `CloseEvidence` is evaluated only in the applied-archive state (F196's rule).
The scopes, checked against the shipped predicate and not assumed. `DurableScope` is `<None />`: `isModuleOwnableWritePath` (`src/lint/core.ts:724`) returns false for every path outside `src/` and for test paths under `src/`, so none of the three write-scope files is module-ownable and `change.graph-anchors-miss-write-scope` cannot fire for the empty anchor set; `scripts/` is lint-ignored (`.ngrace-lint.json` `ignoredDirs`) and no module in `.ngrace/graph/main.xml` owns any of the three files; the spec's `AffectedAreas` names no module and its write-scope Constraint (F136.1's rule) names no `LINKS:` owner for any of them (measured at this plan's commit: zero `LINKS:` occurrences in both script files). The close's move writes five more record files — `findings.xml`, `findings-retired.xml`, `registry-retired.xml`, `decisions.xml`, and `registry.xml` again — but that is the ceremony's write, owned by the authority, not any task's, so they are not in ObservedWriteScope: the observed scope lists observed task writes, and no task below performs any of the close's acts. `rulings.xml` and `rulings-retired.xml` are not listed for the same reason and for their own: under the chartered engine the close's move leaves them byte-identical (measured below), the mode's run on the production record is a registry-only byte write, and no task touches them.
The mode's production run is registry-only in bytes, and the plan says why: the mode re-splices all four live roots, and at any tripwire-consistent record the other three re-splices are byte-identical (the roots invariant — `C-PAYMENT-RECORD-4 roots invariant`, `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:2022` — is green at every committed point; the byte no-op was driven on the production record at this plan's commit, all four live roots sha256-identical). The drifted-record case reddens the byte-invariance criteria and stops the close, which the spec states is the honest outcome.

The row is minted live by the plan and paid by the close's move.` — it names no `F` token and contains no `Closed with` sentence (F197's law: the shipped `closedWithTokens`, `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:338`, mints payments from an archived row's `StatusText` prose, and ordering cannot escape it). The row is inserted after the last live `<Row>` with its own bytes canonical; the pre-existing whitespace drift in the gap before the `</Registry>` close tag (30 spaces, measured) stays untouched by the mint and by the mode — the mode is byte-neutral outside the root attributes line (driven) — and is normalised only by the close, whose pass covers every file the move wrote. Minting the row makes nothing eligible until the bundle is archived: eligibility requires the payer's name to be an archive directory (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:1102`), the live row's name is not one (measured: zero archive directories carry the name), so the plain validator exits 0 after the mint and a `--retire` probe reports `moved 0` — both driven at this plan's commit; the read-back proves the claim rather than asserting it.
The close, stated once and never performed by a task. At the close the ceremony's `--retire` runs for real. The byte-move table below was measured on a pristine clone of this repository at `579b0d5` with a prototype of the chartered engine (the mode, the floor at all four sites, the held unmoved ceilings, the scoped normalising pass), single pass: exactly five of the record files change — `findings.xml`, `findings-retired.xml`, `registry.xml`, `registry-retired.xml`, `decisions.xml` — and `rulings.xml`, `rulings-retired.xml`, `decisions.md` and `record-inventory.json` stay byte-identical to `c1f4dae` (the spec's `AC-RECORD-UNMOVED` set, driven: `git diff --exit-code` over those four paths exits 0 on the moved clone). The probes, discharged at plan time on throwaway copies of the repository (exit codes read directly, never through a pipe; structural counts by the shipped parser, never a grep; every prototype drive ran against a copy of the chartered engine built on a pristine clone at `579b0d5`, and the shipped-engine comparators ran against the shipped engine at the same commit): (G1) the close above, end to end; T-001.Title: Land the chartered engine in scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts — the --rewrite-roots mode, the floored derivation at all four sites, the unmoved-genre window rule, and the move writer's normalising pass — and carry the two suite rewrites and the new engine-observing assertions the change alone reddens

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The mode, wired beside `--retire` in `main()` with the same positional-record-dir convention the shipped modes use, and implemented in `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts` under the maintainer's resolution (`INV-ROOT-WINDOW-MODE-CEILING`): for each of the four live genre roots it derives `base` from the shipped metric read back — `newlineCount` of the whole file for findings and rulings, the live `Row` count (direct `<Row>` children whose status is not retired) for the registry, the live `Entry` count (direct `<Entry>` children whose layer is not retired) for the index — holds the persisted ceiling byte-for-byte (the raw attribute value passes through, never recomputed and never re-serialised), writes `headroom = ceiling − base` through the same root-splice shape the move uses, and re-derives all four live roots or none. It refuses, before any write, with exit 1 and no write, when any live genre's count in its own unit exceeds its persisted ceiling — the message naming the genre, both counts, and the move as the remedy, in the shipped `ceiling-exceeded` shape (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:1540`, mirror it) — and when a live root's ceiling attribute is missing or unreadable. It is a byte no-op on a consistent record (driven on the production record at this plan's commit: all four live roots sha256-identical), it never touches the retired siblings, the stub or the inventory (they carry no root attributes and no shipped writer in this bundle's window touches the stub or the inventory — measured), and it is idempotent: a second run on a rewritten record is again a byte no-op. A hand-raised ceiling is held, never adopted and never recomputed (driven: a registry ceiling of 90 with base 12 and headroom 78 passes through byte-identically) — the laundering boundary the spec's Known-boundary Constraint states, implemented and stated rather than hidden. The refusals were driven at plan time on throwaway copies in both directions and are re-driven by the suite assertions this task adds; the plain validator exits 0 on the production record after the engine change.

The floored derivation and the unmoved-genre window rule, under the maintainer's resolutions. Every headroom derivation site floors its product with `Math.floor`: the two findings sites and the two rulings sites, both the `--split` path (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:596`–`:597`) and the `--retire` path (`:1224`–`:1225`); the registry (15) and index (`INDEX_HEADROOM_ENTRIES`) headrooms are already integers and are not touched. On a successful `--retire` move, a genre with zero moved elements keeps its persisted ceiling and gets its `base` re-derived from its shipped metric read back with `headroom` the remainder; a genre with moved elements keeps the shipped `persistSnapshot` arithmetic with the pre-move base as the ceiling term and the floored headroom; the index is re-derived when its `<Entry>` layers flip and held otherwise. One rule, shared by the move and the mode: the hold path produces `base + headroom = ceiling` with `base` equal to its metric, which is byte-identical to the persisted bytes at any tripwire-consistent record — driven on the production record (byte no-op) and on the synthetic fixture (the unmoved rulings genre byte-identical in values where the shipped engine's clamp rewrites them 60 → 34). Driven on the identical synthetic fixture whose post-move live population is even with differing middles: the shipped engine persists a fractional `ceiling`/`headroom` pair and the chartered engine persists the floored integers, one line tighter — the discriminating drive, both directions on the same fixture bytes (plan-time probe G5/R3). No persisted ceiling is ever written above the previously persisted value (D28): the hold passes through, the clamp takes the smaller term, and the floored term can only tighten.

The normalising pass in the move's writer. For each file the move wrote — a genre with removals, a retired sibling with appends, and the index when its layers flipped — the writer rewrites only the inter-element whitespace to the canonical house shape the split renderer produces: `<newline><two spaces>` before each top-level element and `<newline>` before the root close tag, the bytes after the root close preserved verbatim. Every surviving element's own bytes — the parser-derived spans — pass through byte-identical; the span geometry measured at this commit is what makes this possible (a top-level element's span starts at its `<` byte, so all first-line indent lives in the inter-element gaps). The pass touches no file the move did not write, so a genre with zero moved elements keeps its bytes and the production `rulings.xml`'s five 4-space-indented `<Decision>` elements (`d5.2`, `d6`, `d9.1`, `d19`, `d25` at this plan's commit — F190's drift, measured) stay until a rulings move normalises them — stated, not hidden. Driven on the close clone: after the move, 210 of 210 surviving `<Finding>` elements byte-identical by parse, the appended retired-side elements at 2-space indent with both root close tags at column 0, and the shipped preservation validator exits 0 on the moved record. The pass is byte-neutral on an already-canonical file (the retired siblings' appends confirm it in the same drive).

The suite changes the engine change alone forces, in the same task so the boundary is green. Rewrite `T-001 min not decorative: hand-shrunk findings persist ceiling = Base_live + H without a findings move` (`:738`) in place to the resolution's semantics — renamed to the bundle's house form (`C-ROOT-WINDOW unmoved window: ...`), asserting that a genre with zero moved elements keeps its persisted ceiling with the base re-derived and headroom the remainder, with the shipped clamp scenario kept as the named baseline the assertion overturns and the mutation that turns it red stated (an unmoved genre whose window shrinks across a move in another genre). Re-capture `scripts/fixtures/record-parse/golden/` against the chartered engine's bytes — the bounded one-time reflow, and no other fixture under `scripts/fixtures/record-parse/` changes. Add the engine-observing assertions in the suite's house shape (`isolatedRoot` fixtures, `runValidator`, explicit generous timeouts per F185, payment-invariant forms — no named finding pinned `live`, no ceiling pinned to a number): the mode's byte no-op on a consistent record plus both refusals plus the held hand-raise (the `AC-MODE-SHIPPED` instrument, driving the mode against isolated records, never the production record, with the mutated copies the refusals need); the floor's both-directions drive on the even-population fixture (`AC-ROUNDING-FLOOR`'s instrument, in the `T-001`-fixture shape, the shipped unfloored form shown persisting the fractional value on the identical fixture); the unmoved-genre window across two consecutive moves on isolated records (`AC-WINDOW-UNMOVED`'s instrument, with the byte-identity of the unmoved genre asserted through both); the indent walk over a fixture record before and after a move, asserting element spans byte-identical and the gap shapes, with the named red — a mutated element's own bytes — shown failing on a mutated copy (`AC-INDENT-NORMALISED`'s instrument, plan-time driven: `changed 1` on the mutated copy against `changed 0` clean). At this task's boundary the suite is green as a whole (measured basis: the prototype runs 67/2 before these edits with exactly the two rewritten tests red, and the production record is untouched by this task) and every recorded `Verification` command below exits 0 as written. Nothing here mints a row, writes a `<PaidBy>`, or runs `--retire` against the production record; the row is T-002's.

Byte-invariance and discipline at this task's boundary. This task writes only the two script files — no `src/` file, no record file, no fixture other than the golden re-capture, no `README.md`, no skill, no packaging file. The diffs below are green at this task's boundary (driven at plan time on the clean tree, shapes identical): `src/` and `scripts/` against the base commit with this task's two files excluded; the README/examples/packaging surface; the archive pathset with this bundle's own arrival excluded (F188 — the close renames the bundle's directory itself); and the record directory in full, which this task does not touch. No current-mode lint of this project root appears in this task's `Verification` commands or in the plan's `TargetAssertions`, checked by the rule in the spec's evidence-hygiene Constraint, by hand (F171 — the shipped detector misses the `grace.ts` form): no command text contains `--assertions current`, and none invokes lint of this root omitting `--assertions`. The executor emits its own execution-time cursor events for this task (opened with the epoch open at this task's start, progress, attempt with signature kind and key on fail, verification-unavailable when evidence cannot be collected) and does not omit them; the terminal event, the cursor fold, every gate, the status write, the archive move and the close's own record retirement move are close acts owned by the authority; no task performs any of them and no sentence in this plan implies execution does. Do not hand-write any status.
